sources.entry: _Libraries for visualizing data. Also see awesome-javascript._

summary.one_liner: A curated, link-only list of browser-side JavaScript libraries, tools and resources, organized by category (package managers, bundlers, testing, UI widgets, data visualization, and more).
summary.what_it_does: This is an "awesome" list rather than a software project: it is a long Markdown index of JavaScript libraries and tools grouped under headings such as Package Managers, Bundlers, Testing Frameworks, MVC Frameworks, Data Visualization, Storage, Validation and Machine Learning. Each entry is a one-line description of a project, often with a link. The Data Visualization section, which this copy was listed under in vinta/awesome-python, names charting and graph libraries such as ECharts, D3-based charts, Vega, G2, Cytoscape.js and recharts, and mentions commercial chart libraries without detail. The README is truncated, so the later sections (such as Range Sliders and the rest of the list) were not fully visible. The list points to other awesome lists and a Worth Reading section, but does not itself contain code.
use_cases: Finding a JavaScript charting or graph visualization library
Choosing a front-end testing framework or test runner
Comparing JavaScript bundlers and build tools
Picking a state management or reactive programming library
Finding a browser-side date, string or number utility
Locating UI widgets such as sliders, notifications or tours
notable: Organized into about 90 categories covering nearly every browser-side JavaScript need
Data Visualization section lists dozens of charting, graph and diagramming libraries
Each entry gives a short one-line description of the project
Includes pointers to other awesome lists and a Worth Reading section
caveats: README is truncated, so not every section was visible
Some entries are marked deprecated (e.g. angular.js) and the list may be out of date
Commercial chart libraries are mentioned only by name, with no links or details
